findings.fix: Say what is proved: the rescaled field has the same zeros and the same sign of df(v) (so df < 0 off the zeros is preserved). Drop or qualify 'pseudo-gradient', or prove the IsAdaptedPseudoGradient statement.
findings.issue: The module docstring says 'a pseudo-gradient of f rescales to a pseudo-gradient of f' and (lines 34-36) 'rescales to a complete pseudo-gradient'. The repo's pseudo-gradient notion, IsAdaptedPseudoGradient, also requires the field to be the linear field in a Morse chart near each critical point. The factor (1 + df(v)²)⁻¹ is not 1 near a critical point, so it breaks that condition. Only the zeros and the sign of df are shown to be preserved.

findings.evidence: exists_orderIso_isMIntegralCurve_comp_rateRescale takes hγ : IsMIntegralCurve γ v (a global curve); not_isMIntegralCurveOn_Icc_neg_mgradient_sq_add_pow_four rules out such curves through x₀ ≠ 0.
findings.fix: Remove the trajectory claim for this example or weaken it to 'the same zeros and direction of descent'. Alternatively, prove a reparametrization statement for integral curves on intervals.
findings.issue: The module docstring, and the docstring of isCompleteVectorField_rateRescale_neg_mgradient_sq_add_pow_four, claim that the rescaling of -grad f has 'the same trajectories up to a change of time'. The only reparametrization result, exists_orderIso_isMIntegralCurve_comp_rateRescale, needs a global integral curve of v. This file proves -grad f has no global integral curve through any x₀ ≠ 0, so the cited result covers only the zero trajectory.

summary: The docstrings are accurate on the computations but overclaim twice: they say a pseudo-gradient rescales to a (complete) pseudo-gradient, and they say the rescaled x²+x⁴ field has the same trajectories as -grad f up to a change of time, which no theorem here proves.
